literal: Not despising the power of the capable is, among all protections of those who protect, the head.
translation: Not scorning the power of the capable is the chief of all safeguards for those who guard themselves.
modern: செயல்களைச் செய்து முடிக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களை அவமதிக்காமல் இருப்பது, தம்மைக் காத்துக்கொள்ள விரும்புபவர் செய்யும் காவல்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் சிறந்ததாகும்.
explanation: The couplet emphasizes the importance of respecting powerful and capable people. It states that not scorning their abilities is the most effective way for a person to protect themselves from harm. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to those who have the power to accomplish things, while 'போற்றுவார்' refers to those who wish to guard their own well-being. By placing this respect as the 'head' (தலை) of all protections, the text highlights that avoiding the enmity of the great is the ultimate safeguard.
